submission.natural_language_explanation: L0/N972+ is a context-free, sense-blind single-token detector: it fires when the token at the current position is a degree, rate or accumulation word of the technical register - high, low, dense, densely, thick, thin, tight, tightly, deep, rapid, rapidly, fast, great(ly), highly, heavily, intense, immense, vast, extreme, abundant, porous, saturation, density, congestion, flood, swelling, speed, exponential, increase/increased/increasing, accelerate, escalate, surge, bulk, crowd, steadily, thinly - or one of the short mid-word fragments that lie at the same pole of that embedding direction (en, ens, et, ac, il, ong, el, es, ack, etic), so a rare word the tokenizer splits, such as 'glenoid' or 'Brackenbury', fires on its 'en' piece alone. It ignores the surrounding context and the word's sense ('high school' fires as strongly as 'high pressure'), and it stays silent on colloquial size and quantity words (big, large, huge, enormous, small, tiny, many, few, much, little, plenty), on colloquial rate words (quick, sudden, gradual, abruptly), on the register's category nouns (pressure, temperature, concentration, volume, energy, frequency) and on abstract institutional vocabulary (judiciary, statutory, policy, committee, election, government); its level also rises gently with position, so the same token is weaker in the first two positions of a prompt than mid-prompt.
